what: Woori Financial Group is one of South Korea's four large financial groups. Woori Bank is its main subsidiary, and it has been adding securities and insurance businesses to catch up with its rivals.
customers: South Korean households, small businesses and corporations.
money: Woori Bank deposits, mortgages and corporate lending
recently acquired brokerage and insurance operations
moat: A large Korean deposit base in a market dominated by four groups, though it is the least diversified of the four.
risks: It depends more heavily on banking than its rivals, which makes earnings less diversified
Korean household debt is very high relative to income
Property project financing losses have hurt Korean banks
Only one analyst covers it in this data
opportunities: Analysts see about 27% upside from current levels
Korean governance reform is pushing banks to raise shareholder returns
A dividend yield around 4% with growing buybacks
watch: Credit costs on property project loans and progress in diversifying beyond banking.
